## Today: Adapt A Working Pattern

- Try Plotly hover and zoom on a familiar plot.
- Choose two views that answer connected behavioural questions.
- Adapt data import, filtering, plots and explanations.
- Test that the app supports exploration and survives a fresh session.

Most of the session is building and testing. An own-data prototype is the goal; provided-data practice is available if needed.

## Download And Knit The Workshop Guide {.smaller}

Unzip the whole Week 9 folder into your existing project. Keep scripts beside data/.

Knit **`01_plotly_and_dashboard_workshop.Rmd`**. Read the HTML guide; edit the named R script.

| Task | Script |
|---|---|
| Connect Plotly hover and zoom | `plotly_app.R` |
| Adapt an app to data and a question | `starter_app.R` |

Install plotly once using the guide's installation chunk if needed.

## Does Hover Or Zoom Help The Question? {.smaller}

Hover over a bar or drag to zoom in this plot. Double-click to restore the view.

```{r plotly-demonstration, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
d_demo <- readr::read_csv("data/participant_reaction_times.csv",
                         show_col_types = FALSE)
p_demo <- ggplot2::ggplot(d_demo, ggplot2::aes(x = mean_rt)) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(binwidth = 100) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Participant mean reaction time (ms)",
                y = "Participants")
plotly::ggplotly(p_demo, height = 320)
```

What can you inspect more easily? When would these actions help a behavioural question?

Shiny controls already change the data shown. Plotly adds interaction directly with the plot; useful questions and clear labels still matter.

## Change The Output And Render Pair Together {.smaller}

```{r plotly-ui, eval=FALSE}
# In the UI.
plotlyOutput("rt_plot")
```

```{r plotly-server, eval=FALSE}
# Inside the server.
output$rt_plot <- renderPlotly({
  p <- ggplot(selected_data(), aes(x = mean_rt)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = input$binwidth)
  ggplotly(p)
})
```

p stores the ggplot. ggplotly(p) converts it. Keep the same output name in UI and server.

**Together:** trace the three changed functions, then open `plotly_app.R` and choose **Run App** after completing its blanks.

## Exercise 1: Connect And Test Plotly {.smaller}

Use the guide's **Exercise 1: add hover and zoom** (**10 minutes**).

Complete `plotlyOutput()`, `renderPlotly()` and `ggplotly()` in `plotly_app.R`. Test hover, zoom, group/range filters and recovery from no selection.

The second plot stays a conventional Shiny-reactive plot. Both count as interactive plots for the assessment.

## Start With The Question, Then Choose Views

Before editing, identify:

- What does one row represent?
- Which behavioural question can these variables address?
- What does each of two views contribute?
- What should a user be able to change?
- What remains uncertain or outside the data's scope?

A second plot should add information to the first.

## Choose A Route For The Workshop {.smaller}

**Own data ready:** make two working ggplots outside Shiny, then adapt the supplied app structure.

**Still choosing data:** use `starter_app.R` with the richer provided participant extract. It adds mean response duration and vocabulary score to the familiar reaction times.

The guide gives three question options and a data dictionary. The provided extract is a practice option. Choose and justify a suitable behavioural dataset for your portfolio.

## Two Views Can Answer Connected Questions {.smaller}

For the provided extract, choose:

| Question | Relationship x | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Duration and initiation time | mean_duration | mean_rt |
| Vocabulary score and initiation time | vocabulary_score | mean_rt |
| Vocabulary score and duration | vocabulary_score | mean_duration |

A scatterplot explores the relationship. A boxplot with points explores the outcome by output group.

Check each group's pattern. Association and group differences do not establish causation.

## Exercise 2: Adapt The Pattern {.smaller}

Use **Exercise 2: adapt the app to a question** in the guide.

Provided-data route: complete nine blanks for the data filename, three variable mappings, three axis labels and two explanations. Choose meaningful title and tab names.

Own-data route: adapt the import, columns, control choices, plots and explanations.

Keep shared preparation, two useful plots, and recovery from an empty selection. Work from the supplied structure; no typing along is required.

## Before The Break: Show One Working Selection

Run your app and explain:

- the question and observation unit;
- what each view adds;
- where the group selection enters the shared filter.

If the app does not run, get one output working first. Then restore the second view.

## Use The Second Block To Build And Test

Continue your app. Change one thing at a time.

Test every control, both tabs, empty selections and restoration. Restart R and check that packages and data load without objects left in memory.

If the core works, decide whether Plotly would help either plot. It is an available tool, not a required addition to both views.

## Compare A Design Decision

With a neighbour, compare questions, views and controls.

What pattern becomes easier to inspect because of an interaction? Which explanation or placement could improve the experience?

Record one change and its reason in your own words. This can inform your later reflection.

## The Assessment Combines Report And App {.smaller}

- One behavioural dataset, with its source and observation unit explained.
- Four different static visualisation types in the RMarkdown report, with design commentary.
- A separate Shiny app: meaningful inputs, at least two interactive plots, at most three tabs.
- Reflection on decisions, constraints and limitations.
- A reproducible project and submission ZIP.

Session 10 will practise the separate report/app structure and the extracted-ZIP check.

## After Class: Bring A Working Prototype

Continue toward an own-data app with two meaningful views, clear controls and useful explanations.

If your data are not ready, bring a candidate source and specific questions to Session 10.

Reference: @Wickham2021MasteringShiny, [section 7.1.6](https://mastering-shiny.org/action-graphics.html#interactivity-limitations).

## After Your Attempt: Compare The Examples {.smaller}

`plotly_worked_app.R` completes the Plotly exercise.

`worked_example_app.R` completes one of the provided-data questions. Compare its behaviour and connections with your own choices.

Optional: `extension_app.R` converts both workshop plots to Plotly. Judge whether the extra interaction helps each view. Keep your own version.
